The Ondo State Government has alerted residents to the prevailing heat wave and rising temperatures, urging them to take precautionary measures to protect themselves against heat-related illnesses.
As a precaution, the government advised residents to drink sufficient water regularly, avoid unnecessary exposure to direct sunlight and wear light, comfortable clothing.
The state Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Idowu Ajanaku, gave the advice in a statement issued on Wednesday.
The statement read, “The government advises residents to drink sufficient water regularly to maintain proper body hydration, even when they do not feel thirsty.
“Citizens are also encouraged to avoid unnecessary exposure to direct sunlight, particularly during the hottest periods of the day, and to wear light, comfortable clothing.
“Residents who must go outdoors are advised to make adequate use of umbrellas, hats and other protective coverings to minimise direct exposure to the sun.
“Parents and guardians are equally urged to pay special attention to children, elderly persons and individuals who may be more vulnerable to heat-related illnesses.”
The government also called on school authorities across the state to ensure adequate cross-ventilation in classrooms and other learning environments to reduce heat accumulation.
It urged schools to make clean drinking water readily available and avoid prolonged outdoor activities during periods of intense sunlight.
Residents were further advised to seek prompt medical attention if they experienced symptoms such as dizziness, severe headaches, unusual weakness and excessive sweating.
The statement also encouraged community leaders, market associations, transport operators and other stakeholders to share the safety advisory.
“The Ondo State Government remains committed to the health, safety and well-being of all residents and urges everyone to take these precautionary measures seriously. Public cooperation and responsible behaviour are essential in minimising the impact of the prevailing heat conditions,” Ajanaku said.
The warning comes amid growing concerns about the health risks associated with rising temperatures in Nigeria, as the country prepares for the potential effects of the developing El Niño weather phenomenon.
The National Emergency Management Agency recently warned that the phenomenon could bring hotter temperatures, reduced rainfall, drought, flooding and food shortages, urging Nigerians to stay hydrated, limit outdoor activities during peak heat hours and check on vulnerable people.
El Niño is a climate phenomenon involving unusually warm sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean, which can influence weather patterns around the world.
In an update in October 2026, the Nigerian Meteorological Agency said a strong El Niño event had begun developing, with the likelihood of above-normal temperatures.
NiMet’s 2026 Seasonal Climate Prediction also advised Nigerians to drink water regularly, limit outdoor activities during the hottest periods, stay in shaded areas, use hats and umbrellas, keep homes cool and seek prompt medical attention when necessary.
